title: Withdraws decrement principal by REQUESTED not RECEIVED and have no proportional share cap, converting any peg loss into a winner-takes-all bank run that mixes client share pools

classification.assetImpact: Direct theft of one client's shares by another client. The first client to withdraw during a peg event burns shares from the global share pool that proportionally belong to other clients, leaving later clients with no recoverable balance.
attackPath: 1. Multiple authorized clients (other Behodler protocols) deposit underlying tokens; the strategy swaps each deposit on Curve into vault shares held in a single shared pool.
2. clientBalances tracks principal in underlying units, but the strategy holds a single undivided pile of vault shares.
3. _withdrawInternal computes shares-to-burn as totalShares * requested / totalDeposited and caps only at availableShares (not at the requesting client's pro-rata share).

4. During any peg loss / AMM discount, client A can request a full withdrawal at requested principal, burn enough shares to cover requested (which is more than A's pro-rata share of the depressed pool), receive less than requested in underlying, and decrement A's principal by the full requested amount.
5. Clients B, C still see their full clientBalances on paper but the share pool has been disproportionately depleted by A. Their next withdraw reverts or returns dust.
classification.likelihood: high - any client realising the AMM is discounted is incentivised to race for the exit
classification.assumptions: the strategy holds funds for multiple clients (the documented multi-client model)

justification: Direct theft of client funds via cross-client share pool mixing. Although the requested-vs-received rounding rule is documented, the absence of a per-client proportional share cap is not. Any client can drain shares belonging to other clients with no special conditions beyond a routine peg fluctuation.
rejectionReason: The High severity claim depends on the strategy having multiple competing clients withdrawing in sequence (Alice/Bob bank-run scenario). In the actual deployed topology, each YieldStrategy has only one client at a time (the minter contract), so there is no cross-client share theft. The residual behavior - AMM-realised losses propagating as reduced yield downstream - is the documented and accepted design. The PoC's two-client construction does not correspond to the deployed system.
